principles.instruction: Choose the shared purpose shell before composing a page. Use AppShell for application screens and MarketingHeader for public pages. Document deliberate standalone exceptions.
Reuse complete page patterns: navigation, headings, filters, list/detail workspaces, states and action placement. Reusing controls alone is insufficient.

Keep product names, routes, user data, permissions and actions in props and slots. Shared chrome must remain project agnostic. The marketing header logo is a slot. Every component root exposes data-m-component with the component's name for tests and consumers. It is not a styling hook.
Contribute missing patterns centrally. Do not duplicate source, create repeated local wrappers or apply consumer CSS overrides.

Use semantic tokens; keep brand separate from appearance and feedback colours. Verify every supported theme. Accent is a brand token, separate from ink, surface, and the feedback colours. Brands declare only the --m-brand-* contract (--m-brand-l-*, --m-brand-d-* and the brand fonts); each appearance resolves --m-accent, --m-on-accent, --m-accent-fill, the surfaces and their --m-inv-* twins from it, so every brand gets both without brand-specific CSS. A runtime brand comes from ThemeProvider brandTokens. CallToAction and a featured Pricing card use the page surface unless tone="inverse" opts into the inverse token remap. ThemeProvider scope="container" paints those tokens on a wrapper and leaves the document unchanged. The default scope is document.

Verify responsive layout, accessible names, keyboard operation, focus and loading/empty/error states. Automated checks alone cannot prove visual quality. A plan that is not available exposes a status and does not offer a purchase link. Column titles accept an explicit heading level so a page can keep a single h1.
